readings.title: The First and the Last
readings.subtitle: “Besides Me there is no Elohim.”
readings.text: [Isaiah 44:6] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Sovereign of Yisra’ěl, and his Redeemer, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am the First and <dn>I</dn> am the Last, besides <dn>Me</dn> there is no <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [7] <dq>And who is like <dn>Me</dn>? Let him call and declare it, and lay it before <dn>Me</dn>, since <dn>I</dn> appointed the everlasting people. And the events that are coming and those that do come, let them declare these to them.</dq> [8] <dq>Do not fear, nor be afraid. Have <dn>I</dn> not since made you hear, and declared it? You are <dn>My</dn> witnesses. Is there an Eloah besides <dn>Me</dn>? There is no other Rock, <dn>I</dn> know not one.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Folly of Idolatry
readings.subtitle: A man makes a god from the rest of a log used for firewood.
readings.text: [Isaiah 44:9] Those who make an idol, all of them are emptiness, and their delights do not profit. And they are their own witnesses; they neither see nor know, so that they are put to shame. [10] Who would form a mighty one or cast an idol that is of no value? [11] See, all his companions are ashamed, and the workmen, they are but men. Let them all be gathered together, let them stand up, let them fear, let them be put to shame, altogether. [12] The craftsman in iron with the tools works one in the coals, and fashions it with hammers, and works it with the strength of his arms. Even so, he shall be hungry, and has no strength; he drinks no water and is weary. [13] The carpenter stretches out his rule, he outlines it with chalk; he fashions it with a plane, and he outlines it with the compass, and makes it like the figure of a man, according to the comeliness of a man, to remain in the house. [14] He cuts down cedars for himself, and takes cypress and oak, which he raised among the trees of the forest. He has planted a pine, and the rain nourishes it. [15] And it shall be for a man to burn, for he takes some of it and warms himself. He also kindles it and shall bake bread. He also makes a mighty one and bows himself to it – has made it a carved image and falls down before it. [16] Half of it he shall burn in the fire; with this half he eats meat. He roasts a roast, and is satisfied. He also warms himself and says, “Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire.” [17] And the rest of it he makes into a mighty one, his carved image. He falls down before it and worships, prays to it and says, “Deliver me, for you are my mighty one.” [18] They do not know nor understand, for <dn>He</dn> has smeared their eyes from seeing, and their hearts from understanding. [19] And no one recalls it to his heart, nor is there knowledge nor understanding to say, “I have burned half of it in the fire, and I have also baked bread on its coals; I have roasted meat and eaten it. And shall I make <dn>את</dn> the rest of it an abomination? Should I fall down before a log of wood?” [20] Feeding on ashes, a deceived heart turns him aside, and he does not deliver <dn>את</dn> his being, nor says, “Is there not a lie in my right hand?”

readings.title: Remember and Return
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH, the Redeemer, names His shepherd, Koresh.
readings.text: [Isaiah 44:21] <dq>“Remember these matters, O Ya‛aqoḇ, and Yisra’ěl, for you are <dn>My</dn> servant! <dn>I</dn> have formed you, you are <dn>My</dn> servant, O Yisra’ěl, do not forget <dn>Me</dn>!</dq> [22] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall wipe out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to <dn>Me</dn>, for <dn>I</dn> shall redeem you.”</dq> [23] Sing, O heavens, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall do it! Shout, O depths of the earth! Break forth into singing, O mountains, forest, and every tree in it! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall redeem Ya‛aqoḇ, and make Himself clear in Yisra’ěl. [24] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, your Redeemer, and <dn>He</dn> who formed you from the womb, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, doing all, stretching out the heavens all alone, spreading out the earth, with none beside <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [25] <dq>frustrating the signs of the babblers, and driving diviners mad, turning wise men backward, and making their knowledge foolish,</dq> [26] <dq>confirming the word of <dn>His</dn> servant, and completing the counsel of <dn>His</dn> messengers, who says of Yerushalayim, ‘Be inhabited,’ and of the cities of Yehuḏah, ‘They shall be built, and her ruins raised up by <dn>Me</dn>,’</dq> [27] <dq>who is saying to the deep, ‘Be dry, and your rivers <dn>I</dn> dry up,’</dq> [28] <dq>who is saying of Koresh, ‘<dn>He</dn> is <dn>My</dn> shepherd, and he completes all <dn>My</dn> pleasure, even saying to Yerushalayim, “Let her be built,” and to the Hěḵal, “Let her foundation be laid.” ’</dq>

readings.title: The Commission of Koresh
readings.subtitle: “I am YeHoVaH, and there is none else.”
readings.text: [Isaiah 45:1] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to <dn>His</dn> anointed, to Koresh, whose right hand <dn>I</dn> have strengthened, to subdue nations before him and ungird the loins of sovereigns, to open before him the double doors, so that gates are not shut: [2] <dq><dn>I</dn> go before you and make the crooked places straight; <dn>I</dn> shatter the gates of bronze and cut down the bars of iron.</dq> [3] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give you the treasures of darkness and hoarded wealth of secret places, so that you know that <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who are calling you by your name, am the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl.</dq> [4] <dq>For the sake of Ya‛aqoḇ <dn>My</dn> servant, and of Yisra’ěl <dn>My</dn> chosen, <dn>I</dn> also call you by your name, <dn>I</dn> give you a title, though you have not known <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [5] <dq><dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and there is none else – there is no <dn>Elohim</dn> besides <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> gird you, though you have not known <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [6] <dq>so that they know from the rising of the sun to its setting that there is none but <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and there is none else,</dq> [7] <dq>forming light and creating darkness, making peace and creating evil. <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do all these.’</dq>

readings.title: The Potter and the Clay
readings.subtitle: “Woe to him who strives with his Maker!”
readings.text: [Isaiah 45:8] <dq>“Rain down, O heavens, from above, and let clouds pour down righteousness. Let the earth open, let them bring forth deliverance, and let righteousness spring up together. <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have created it.</dq> [9] “Woe to him who strives with his Maker! (a potsherd with the potsherds of the earth). Does clay say to him who forms it, ‘What are you making?’ Or your handiwork say, ‘He has no hands’? [10] “Woe to him who says to his father, ‘What are you bringing forth?’ Or to the woman, ‘What are you labouring over?’ ” [11] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl, and his Maker, <dq>“Do you ask <dn>Me</dn> about <dn>My</dn> sons what is to come? And about the work of <dn>My</dn> hands do you command <dn>Me</dn>?</dq> [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have made the earth, and created man on it. <dn>I</dn>, <dn>My</dn> hands have stretched out the heavens, and all their host <dn>I</dn> have commanded.</dq> [13] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have stirred him up in righteousness, and all his ways <dn>I</dn> make straight. <dn>He</dn> builds <dn>My</dn> city and lets <dn>My</dn> exiles go, not for price nor reward,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.

readings.title: Nations Turn to Israel's God
readings.subtitle: “Indeed, Ěl is in you, and there is none else.”
readings.text: [Isaiah 45:14] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“The labour of Mitsrayim and merchandise of Kush and of the Seḇaites, men of size, come over to you and they are yours. They walk behind you, they come over in chains, and they bow down to you. They make supplication to you, saying, ‘Indeed, <dn>Ěl</dn> is in you, and there is none else, no mighty one.’ ”</dq> [15] Truly You are <dn>Ěl</dn>, who hide Yourself, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, Saviour! [16] They shall be put to shame, and even be humiliated, all of them – the makers of idols shall go away together in humiliation. [17] Yisra’ěl shall be saved by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with an everlasting deliverance. You are not to be ashamed nor hurt, forever and ever.

readings.title: A Call to the Ends of the Earth
readings.subtitle: “Turn to Me and be saved.”
readings.text: [Isaiah 45:18] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Creator of the heavens, <dn>He</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn>, Former of earth and its Maker, <dn>He</dn> established it, <dn>He</dn> did not create it to be empty, <dn>He</dn> formed it to be inhabited: <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and there is none else.</dq> [19] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth. <dn>I</dn> have not said to the seed of Ya‛aqoḇ, ‘Seek <dn>Me</dn> in vain.’ <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, speaking righteousness, declaring matters that are straight.</dq> [20] <dq>“Gather yourselves and come; draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations. No knowledge have they who are lifting up <dn>את</dn> the wood of their carved image, and pray to a mighty one that does not save.</dq> [21] <dq>“Declare and bring near, let them even take counsel together. Who has announced this from of old? Who has declared it from that time? Is it not <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? And there is no mighty one besides <dn>Me</dn>, a righteous <dn>Ěl</dn> and a Saviour, there is none besides <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [22] <dq>“Turn to <dn>Me</dn> and be saved, all you ends of the earth! For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl</dn>, and there is none else.</dq> [23] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have sworn by <dn>Myself</dn>, a word has gone out of <dn>My</dn> mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, so that to <dn>Me</dn> every knee shall bow, every tongue swear.</dq> [24] <dq>“One shall say, ‘Only in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do <dn>I</dn> have righteousness and strength’ – he comes to <dn>Him</dn>. And all those displeased with <dn>Him</dn> shall be put to shame.</dq> [25] <dq>“In <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the seed of Yisra’ěl shall be declared right and boast.”</dq>

readings.title: The Burden of Idols
readings.subtitle: “They were unable to deliver the burden, but they themselves went into captivity.”
readings.text: [Isaiah 46:1] Běl has bowed down, Neḇo is stooping, their idols were on the beasts and on the cattle. That which is carried is burdensome, a burden to the weary. [2] They have stooped, they have bowed down together, they were unable to deliver the burden, but they themselves went into captivity. [3] <dq>“Listen to <dn>Me</dn>, O house of Ya‛aqoḇ, and all the remnant of the house of Yisra’ěl, who are borne from the belly, who are carried from the womb:</dq> [4] <dq>even to your old age, <dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn>, and even to grey hairs <dn>I</dn> carry! <dn>I</dn> have made and <dn>I</dn> bear, and <dn>I</dn> carry and rescue.</dq> [5] <dq>“To whom do you liken <dn>Me</dn>, and compare <dn>Me</dn> and make <dn>Me</dn> similar, that we should be alike?</dq> [6] <dq>“They pour gold out of the bag, and weigh silver on the scale. They hire a goldsmith, and he makes it a mighty one. They fall down, they also bow themselves.</dq> [7] <dq>“They bear it on the shoulder, they carry it and set it in its place, and it stands – from its place it does not move. Though one cries out to it, it does not answer, nor save him from his distress.</dq>

readings.title: Remember the Former Events
readings.subtitle: “I am Ěl, and there is no one else.”
readings.text: [Isaiah 46:8] <dq>“Remember this, and show yourselves men; turn it back, you transgressors.</dq> [9] <dq>“Remember the former events of old, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl</dn>, and there is no one else – <dn>Elohim</dn>, and there is no one like <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [10] <dq>declaring the end from the beginning, and from of old that which has not yet been done, saying, ‘<dn>My</dn> counsel does stand, and all <dn>My</dn> delight <dn>I</dn> do,’</dq> [11] <dq>calling a bird of prey from the east, the man who executes <dn>My</dn> counsel, from a distant land. Indeed <dn>I</dn> have spoken it, <dn>I</dn> also bring it to pass. <dn>I</dn> have planned it, <dn>I</dn> also do it.</dq> [12] <dq>“Listen to <dn>Me</dn>, you stubborn-hearted, who are far from righteousness:</dq> [13] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall bring <dn>My</dn> righteousness near, it is not far off, and <dn>My</dn> deliverance, it is not delayed. And <dn>I</dn> shall give deliverance in Tsiyon, <dn>My</dn> esteem to Yisra’ěl.</dq>

readings.title: The Humiliation of Babylon
readings.subtitle: “Sit on the ground without a throne, O daughter of the Kasdim!”
readings.text: [Isaiah 47:1] “Come down and sit in the dust, O maiden daughter of Baḇel. Sit on the ground without a throne, O daughter of the Kasdim! For no more do they call you tender and delicate. [2] “Take the millstones and grind flour. Remove your veil, lift up the skirt, uncover the leg, pass through rivers. [3] “Let your nakedness be uncovered, let your shame also be exposed. I take vengeance, and meet no man.” [4] Our Redeemer, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name, the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl. [5] <dq>“Sit silent, and go into darkness, O daughter of Kasdim! For no more do they call you Mistress of Reigns.</dq> [6] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> was wroth with <dn>My</dn> people, <dn>I</dn> have profaned <dn>My</dn> inheritance and <dn>I</dn> gave them into your hand. You showed them no compassion, you made your yoke very heavy on the elderly.</dq> [7] <dq>“And you said, ‘<dn>I</dn> am mistress forever,’ so that you did not take these matters to heart, and did not remember the latter end of them.</dq>

readings.title: Judgment on Babylon's Pride
readings.subtitle: “Evil shall come upon you, you not knowing from where it arises.”
readings.text: [Isaiah 47:8] <dq>“And now, hear this, you who are given to pleasures, who dwells complacently, who says in your heart, ‘<dn>I</dn> am, and there is none but me. <dn>I</dn> do not sit as a widow, nor do <dn>I</dn> know the loss of children.’</dq> [9] <dq>“Both of these come to you suddenly, in one day: the loss of children, and widowhood. They shall come upon you in completeness, because of your many witchcrafts, for your numerous great potent spells.</dq> [10] <dq>“And you have trusted in your evil, you have said, ‘No one sees me.’ Your wisdom and your knowledge have led you astray. And you have said in your heart, ‘<dn>I</dn> am, and there is none but me.’</dq> [11] <dq>“But evil shall come upon you, you not knowing from where it arises, and trouble fall upon you, you being unable to put it off, and ruin come upon you suddenly, which you know not.</dq> [12] <dq>“Stand now with your potent spells and your many witchcrafts, in which you have laboured from your youth, if so be you are able to profit, if so be you find strength.</dq> [13] <dq>“You are exhausted by your many counsels; let the astrologers, the stargazers, and those who prognosticate by the new moons stand up and save you from what is coming upon you.</dq> [14] <dq>“See, they shall be as stubble, fire shall burn them, they do not deliver themselves from the power of the flame, there is not a coal to be warmed by, nor a fire to sit before it!</dq> [15] <dq>“So they shall be to you with whom you have laboured, your merchants from your youth. They shall wander, each one his own way, there is none to save you.</dq>

readings.title: Israel's Stubbornness
readings.subtitle: “I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.”
readings.text: [Isaiah 48:1] <dq>“Hear this, O house of Ya‛aqoḇ, who are called by the name of Yisra’ěl, and have come from the waters of Yehuḏah, who swear by the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and profess the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl – though not in truth or in righteousness –</dq> [2] <dq>for they call themselves after the set-apart city, and lean on the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name:</dq> [3] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have declared the former events from the beginning, and they went forth from <dn>My</dn> mouth, and <dn>I</dn> made you hear them. Suddenly <dn>I</dn> acted, and they came to be.</dq> [4] <dq>“Because <dn>I</dn> knew that you were hard, and your neck was an iron sinew, and your forehead bronze,</dq> [5] <dq>therefore <dn>I</dn> declared it to you long ago. Before it came <dn>I</dn> made you hear, lest you should say, ‘<dn>My</dn> idol has done them, and <dn>My</dn> carved image and <dn>My</dn> moulded image commanded them.’</dq> [6] <dq>“You have heard, look at them all. And do you not declare it? From now on <dn>I</dn> shall make you hear new ones, even hidden ones, which you have not known.</dq> [7] <dq>“Now they shall be created and not long ago. And before this day you have not heard them, lest you should say, ‘Look, <dn>I</dn> knew them.’</dq> [8] <dq>“No, you have not heard; no, you have not known; no, from of old your ear has not been open. Because <dn>I</dn> knew that you are indeed treacherous, and are called ’a transgressor from the womb.’</dq> [9] <dq>“For <dn>My</dn> Name’s sake <dn>I</dn> postponed <dn>My</dn> displeasure, and for <dn>My</dn> praise <dn>I</dn> held it back from you, so as not to cut you off.</dq> [10] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> have refined you, but not as silver; <dn>I</dn> have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.</dq> [11] <dq>“For <dn>My</dn> own sake, for <dn>My</dn> own sake, <dn>I</dn> do it. For how is it profaned? And <dn>My</dn> esteem <dn>I</dn> do not give to another.</dq>
